abstract: Addition and multiplication of integers each generate an algebra of sequences: power series and Dirichlet series. We represent each by infinite matrices of zeros and ones, called here Hrvatska (the powers of the shift) and Konavle (the floor-quotient matrices), and prove that each is the unique representation in which every row sums to a partial sum of the series (Theorems 1 and 2). In Konavle the coefficient $a_k$ sits in column $\lfloor n/k\rfloor$ of row $n$, so the floor function is forced. The floor-quotient matrices, their restriction to the set $LL(n)$ of floor quotients of $n$, and the inverse pair representing $\zeta$ and $1/\zeta$ are due to J.-P. Cardinal and to Lagarias and Montague; we present them in mirrored coordinates, with Euler products that hold entry by entry for $\zeta$ and for Dedekind zeta functions of quadratic fields, and claim no priority for them. Our second contribution is the sieved walk (Theorem 7): splitting the Euler factors of the primes dividing $P$ off the operator of $\zeta$ gives an identity that computes the Mertens function on the part of $LL(n)$ reached by quotients coprime to $P$, a set of at most $2\sqrt{\delta n}+2^{\omega-1}$ elements, where $\delta=\prod_{p\mid P}(1-1/p)$. For $P=2$ its length is $\sqrt{2n}$ up to a bounded term, as also follows from a theorem of Heyman and Miraj; since $\delta$ tends to zero, for fixed $P$ and large $n$ the walk is shorter than any prescribed fraction of $LL(n)$. We say what the Riemann Hypothesis is in this language and what it is not, and record a conjecture of the first author that would imply it and is in fact stronger. Nothing towards it is proved, and no progress towards the Riemann Hypothesis is claimed.
author: lasic_oblak
change_summary: Revision after the review of submission RS4MuwhpRC8QyC4V. (1) Theorem 7(d): the counting error in the proof is corrected (the number of odd m with m(m+2) <= 2n is the integer part of sqrt(2n+1)/2, at least sqrt(2n)/2 - 1); the final bound is unchanged. (2) Heyman and Miraj, On Some Floor Function Sets, is cited as [21]; the asymptotic sqrt(2n)+O(1) for the odd-denominator set is attributed to their Theorem 3(i), and part (d) is no longer claimed as new. (3) The corollary is restated for fixed P and sufficiently large n, with the remark that it is not uniform in n. (4) The scope statement in Section 9 is narrowed: Sections 2 to 7 hold for every sequence; Theorems 6 and 7 use the Moebius sequence as the inverse of the sequence of ones. (5) The sentence about numerical testing of the conjecture is removed. (6) The introduction states what remains new after comparison with the literature, and that no computational advantage over Hurst's algorithm is claimed. (7) A closing note records how the work came about. No new theorem is added in this revision.
title: The Zeta Enigma: Hrvatska and Konavle, Two Croatian Representations of Addition and Multiplication
